 Shnaider Will Play Fernandez for Tokyo Title
 Diana Shnaider will play for her sixth career title vs. Leylah Fernandez in an all-lefty Tokyo final.
 Richard Pagliaro October 31, 2026 2 minute read 
 Share X Facebook WhatsApp Email Copy link More… 
 Listen to this article 
 1× 
 ✕ 
 By Richard Pagliaro | Saturday, October 31, 2026
 Photo credit: Screen Shot
 The Tokyo final will take a left-handed turn.
 Diana Shnaider defeated 18-year-old wild card Mia Pohankova 6-4, 7-6(7) to advance to her first final of the season at the Toray Pan Pacific Open.
 The third-seeded Shnaider set up an all-lefty Tokyo final against a red-hot Leylah Fernandez.
 Earlier, Fernandez swept lucky loser Kamilla Rakhimova 7-5, 6-3, to reach her 11th career final. 
 A resurgent Fernandez has won 16 of her last 20 matches and will play for her seventh career championship tomorrow.
 One round after Shnaider fought off Alexandra Eala, 2-6, 7-6(5), 6-4, she rose up to pass another tight test against the hard-hitting Pohankova, who had scored back-to-back wins over Naomi Osaka and Alycia Parks.
 Facing a 2-4 deficit in today’s second semifinal, Shnaider dialed in her drives, amped up her aggression and reeled off five consecutive games. Shnaider won eight of the final 10 points to snatch a one-set lead.
 In the second set tie break, Shnaider saved a set point at 5-6. Shnaider converted her second match point securing a spot in her seventh Tour-level final.
 It is Shnaider’s first final since she collected the Monterrey title in August of 2025. Roland Garros semifinalist Shnaider will play for her sixth career title. 
 Shnaider carries a 3-2 career edge over 2021 US Open finalist Fernandez, including winning their last three meetings.
